display.purpose: the tooltip title (zone name, "Exile Companion", settings group name). Truncates on one line.

subtitle.purpose: the line under the title. On the overlay it carries act, class level and step.

body-sm.purpose: the "Then:" line, one step under the current actions so they win the first glance. Quick menu rows, "route didn't load".

label.purpose: the compact zone line, "Nothing to do here", settings row labels and values, the move bar's "Exile Companion".

button.purpose: every button. Selects set their value at 13px.

flavour.purpose: route hints, the startup notice, the missing-log hint (upright).

caption.purpose: settings explanations. Upright for bind errors.

key-hint.purpose: shortcut names next to buttons and menu rows, the move bar hint, replay line count.

narrative.northStar: The Item Tooltip of Where You Stand
narrative.overview:
Every surface Exile Companion draws is a Path of Exile item tooltip. The zone is the item name in a tinted header band, the things to do there are its properties, and the way out is the last line, "Then:". The overlay, the quick menu and each settings group use the same parts. There's a see-through black body with no frame, a header band with rules along both edges and wedge ends that meet in a diamond, short glowing separators, centered small caps, and text colours that mean what they mean in the game.

The system is dense and quiet. It is read in glances over a busy, dark game scene, so it has no fills, gradients or accents beyond what the game's own tooltips carry, and colour is spent only on meaning. A boss name is red because the game's corrupted red is the danger colour, a waypoint is blue because it is magic. The overlay window is transparent and fitted to its content. Only the plate paints. The settings window has no system frame. It has a title bar like the overlay's move bar, a 1px Edge window edge, and groups that are still tooltips standing on a dark ground.

It rejects the web-app card (rounded corners, drop shadows, coloured buttons) and the generic brown-and-gold fantasy panel. The chrome is neutral grey and black. The only warm hue in the frame is Currency Sand in the header bands.
keyCharacteristics: See-through black bodies, opacity set by the player (70 to 100 percent on the overlay, lower washes out over bright scenes).
A header band per tooltip, tinted by kind, with 1px rules along its top and bottom edges and, at each end, a wedge drawn from both corners to a 7px diamond on the middle.
Alegreya Sans SC at medium weight for all tooltip text. Alegreya Sans italic for flavour.

rules.name: The Game's Meaning Rule
rules.body: A hue appears only where the game uses it for the same meaning. New content picks the matching item text colour. If the game has none for that meaning, it stays grey or white.

rules.name: The Grey Ladder Rule
rules.body: Brightness is rank. Label Grey is for what something is, Plain Grey for running text, Normal Item White for chrome, Value White for what the player acts on. On the overlay every grey starts one step up, at Plain Grey, because the plate sits over snow and bright light as often as over dark ground. Label Grey stays for the menu and settings, which have their own dark ground.

rules.name: The Tint by Kind Rule
rules.body: One tint per tooltip drives its band, frame, diamonds and separators together. Every header uses Currency Sand, which sits well on the black body. Towns are told apart by the "town" subtitle. Buttons and focus stay neutral grey.

rules.name: The Small Caps Voice Rule
rules.body: Everything in a tooltip is Alegreya Sans SC at 500. Switch to Alegreya Sans for flavour (italic) and for literal strings like key names, file paths and speed multipliers.

rules.name: The Size as Rank Rule
rules.body: The current actions are the largest body text (15px) and the brightest. The zone line and labels drop to 13px grey. Key hints sit at 11px. Do not add a size between these steps.

rules.name: The No Frame Rule
rules.body: A tooltip body has no border and no shadow. The only frame is the pair of 1px tint rules inside the header band, 2px from its top and bottom and stopping 40px short of each end. The one exception is state. An unlocked overlay gets a 1px Normal Item White outline at 60 percent, 2px out, while it can be dragged.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Nothing is rounded. Ornament lives only in the header's wedge ends and their diamonds. Every line in it meets another.

dos: Do build every new panel as a tooltip, with a header band tinted by kind over a see-through black body with no frame.

Do colour route content only with the game's item text colours, by meaning (Magic Blue for waypoints and portals, Corrupted Red for bosses, Quest Green for quests, Unique Brown for trials and arenas, Gem Teal for gems).
Do keep the overlay's bottom center fixed and let new content grow upward.
Do set tooltip text in Alegreya Sans SC 500 and switch to Alegreya Sans for flavour, key names and paths.
Do draw small marks as inline SVG in currentColor.
Do show state on buttons with the pressed treatment (Normal Item White border, Value White text), not with a fill colour.
donts: Don't round corners or add drop shadows. The system is square and flat.
Don't put a border around a tooltip body. The frame belongs to the header band.
